question: Can an LLM be trained with RL on unlabeled test data, with rewards estimated by the model's own majority vote?
hypothesis: Test-time-scaling signals such as majority voting give rewards good enough to drive RL without ground-truth labels.
contributions: Introduce TTRL, RL on unlabeled data with majority-voting rewards
Show consistent gains across models and tasks and that TTRL can exceed the initial maj@n
Analysis of why it works and when it fails

method.summary: GRPO is run on each benchmark's unlabeled questions. 64 samples per question vote for a label; reward is 1 if a sampled answer equals the majority answer, else 0; 32 of the samples are used for training. Evaluation is pass@1 on the same benchmark.
method.task: RL for mathematical/scientific reasoning without labels (test-time training)

datasets.name: AIME 2024
datasets.size: inferred: 30 problems (AIME benchmark; not stated in text)
datasets.split: test questions without labels used for TTRL; same set evaluated

datasets.name: MATH-500
datasets.split: same as above; also split into 5 difficulty levels for Table 3

training.objective: GRPO with majority-vote rule-based reward (Eq 3); PPO and PRIME also tried on MATH-500

other.rollout: 64 responses sampled for voting, downsampled to 32 per prompt for training
other.note: batch size, KL coefficient, clip range not stated; Fig 11 failure used train batch 256
other.training_data_size: equals the benchmark dataset size (Table 4 caption)

inference.decoding: sampling for main results; greedy for analysis and Qwen2.5-Math additional experiments (Table 4, Fig 4, Fig 8)
inference.samples: 16 responses per question (4 for 32k context); avg@64/maj@64 in Fig 7

metrics.name: pass@1
metrics.definition: mean over k samples of correctness p_i

metrics.name: maj@n
metrics.definition: accuracy of majority-voted answer over n samples

metrics.name: label accuracy / reward accuracy
metrics.definition: whether estimated label matches truth / fraction of majority rewards equal to ground-truth rewards

baselines: RL (leakage): RL on test data with ground-truth labels
eval.protocol: TTRL applied to each benchmark individually, then evaluated on that benchmark; no held-out set, no seeds or significance tests stated.

limits: Authors concede it is an initial exploration; prior-knowledge and hyperparameter impacts need deeper analysis, ablations promised in future revisions
Trains and evaluates on the same unlabeled test questions (transductive); the comparison with models trained on large labeled sets is called unfair by the authors
Fails with wrong temperature/episodes or when prior knowledge is insufficient (harder MATH-500 levels gain less)
GPQA and some instruct models (Mistral-Nemo AIME) get worse or no gain
No seeds, variance or batch size/KL settings reported

terms.definition: for an incorrectly predicted answer, even if the estimated label does not match the ground truth label, as long as it differs from the predicted answer, the verifier will still output a negative reward
performing RL directly on the test data with ground-truth labels
